newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada natural gas sales rise in March.
newsitem.headline: Canada natural gas sales rise in March.

text.p: Canadian sales of natural gas rose 1.5 percent in March from a year earlier to a total of 7.32 billion cubic metres, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
The federal agency said higher demand by electric utilities and the chemical industry led to a 6.7 increase in industrial sector sales, including direct sales.

This rise more than offset lower sales to the residential sector, which fell 3.4 percent, and to the commercial sector, which dropped 2.5 percent. Sales to both sectors fell due to warmer than normal weather throughout most of the country, StatsCan said.

Year-to-date sales fell 0.4 percent from March 1996, the agency said. Decreased sales to the residential sector, down 2.9 percent, and to the commercial sector, off 3.7 percent, were mainly due to the near normal temperatures in the first three months of 1997, compared with last year's colder temperatures.
Year-to-date sales to the industrial sector continued to grow, posting a 3.3 percent increase from the same period last year, StatCan said.
(For more information from Statistics Canada, contact Gary Smalldridge at 613-951-3567, Construction and Energy Division).
